attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The finite-matrix tangent lemma is valid, but Yang-Mills still has to supply the boundary OPE expansion and compute H,K for locked reflected Wilson hairpins.
steps: Lock a finite Wilson collar family F_i^delta and form the continuum collar OS matrix N_delta, which is positive by the closed-cone argument.
Separate the multiplicative reflected-boundary hairpin factor B_delta from N_delta; the intended same-theory OS matrix is q_delta=hat N_delta oslash hat B_delta.
Assume a boundary OPE scale eta(delta) with q_eta=E+eta H+eta^2K+o(eta^2), E=11^*.
Decompose C^n=span{1} direct-sum 1^perp and use P=I-E/n.
The scalar rank-one block is 1^*q_eta1=n^2+O(eta), hence positive for small eta.
The Schur complement on 1^perp is S_eta=eta PHP+eta^2(PKP-n^{-2}PH11^*HP)+o(eta^2).
Therefore any negative vector for PHP, or any negative Schur-corrected second-order vector in ker(PHP), gives a negative principal determinant for q_eta at small eta.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: Reflection positivity of collar matrices N_delta is known formally, but OS positivity of the intended plane observables depends on q_delta. Without proving that the extracted B_delta is same-theory and that the expansion is controlled in the RG topology, the tangent conditions are only a diagnostic.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Wilson quotient tangent-cone test for OS positivity

assumptions: The additive boundary contact has already been eliminated or proved zero on the diagonal-positive OS block.
Diagonal entries of N_delta and B_delta are positive and B_delta has no zero entries on the finite block.
There is an asymptotic scale eta(delta)->0 such that q_eta=E+eta H+eta^2 K+o(eta^2) in operator norm.
The all-ones convention E=11^* is used; P=I-E/n projects to 1^perp.
definitions: source object: finite collar OS blocks N_delta for locked gauge-invariant Wilson observables, a multiplicative boundary Gram block B_delta, and their diagonal normalizations.
target object: OS-positive continuum Schwinger matrices for the unmodified Wilson observables at the reflection plane, encoded by q_delta=\widehat N_delta\oslash\widehat B_delta.
controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions, reduced after collar passage to finite Schur-preimage positivity of q_delta.

same-theory condition: B_delta may remove only collar artifacts already contained in the locked Wilson renormalization; no new boundary counterterm, algebra enlargement, or pair-dependent observable redefinition is allowed.

equations.label: same-theory quotient
equations.valid_when: The boundary anomaly is multiplicative and the diagonal normalization is part of the locked observable convention.

equations.label: rank-one boundary expansion
equations.valid_when: The reflected Wilson boundary OPE has a two-term finite-block asymptotic in the cutoff-removal topology.

equations.label: first tangent gate
equations.valid_when: q_eta is positive semidefinite for all sufficiently small eta>0.

equations.label: second tangent gate
equations.valid_when: R is the orthogonal projection onto ker(PHP) inside 1^perp; equivalently, with e=n^{-1/2}1, the correction is n^{-1}PHee^*HP.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find y in 1^perp with y^*Hy<0, or y in ker(PHP) with y^*(PKP-n^{-2}PH11^*HP)y<0.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Finite-dimensional bridge from Wilson boundary OPE coefficients to OS positivity or to an explicit determinant falsifier.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Finite Wilson collar quotient blocks near the rank-one matrix have a valid second-order OS tangent-cone test. If q_eta=E+eta H+eta^2 K+o(eta^2), E=11^*, is the same-theory quotient OS matrix, then q_eta>=0 for all small eta>0 forces PHP>=0 on 1^perp and, on ker(PHP), the Schur-corrected form PKP-n^{-2}PH11^*HP is nonnegative. A negative value is a finite Wilson falsifier.

assumptions: D_eta=I+eta A+O(eta^2) with A diagonal, or the block has first been diagonally normalized to return q_0=E.
The diagonal congruence is same-theory: it is fixed by individual Wilson-loop renormalizations, not by pair-dependent boundary data.
The finite rank-one block 1^*q_eta1 stays positive.
definitions: one-body collar renormalization: a nonsingular diagonal D_eta multiplying each Wilson observable before diagonal normalization.
coboundary tangent: a first-order matrix of the form a1^*+1a^*+lambda E.
Schur complement test: positivity of q_eta is equivalent to positivity of Pq_etaP-Pq_eta1(1^*q_eta1)^{-1}1^*q_etaP once the rank-one block is positive.

equations.label: first-order coboundary
equations.valid_when: q'_eta is obtained from q_eta by a valid one-body diagonal congruence and re-normalization.

equations.label: zero-sum invariance
equations.valid_when: P1=0, so all coboundary terms vanish on the OS null tangent space.

equations.label: Schur-complement invariant sign
equations.valid_when: The scalar rank-one block is positive; signs of leading nonzero coefficients of S_eta are invariant under same-theory diagonal congruence.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If a supposed obstruction disappears after a permitted diagonal congruence, it was not a same-theory falsifier.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Prevents declaring a removable one-body normalization a falsifier; only zero-sum or Schur-corrected negativity is meaningful.
candidate_lemmas.statement: The first nonzero tangent obstruction is invariant under harmless one-body Wilson renormalizations. Diagonal congruences and rephasings change H by coboundary terms that vanish on 1^perp, and the Schur complement formulation preserves the sign of the first nonzero obstruction.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if no valid same-theory multiplicative B_delta or finite-block boundary OPE can be defined for Wilson collars.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if H is nonnegative on 1^perp and the Schur-corrected K is nonnegative on ker(PHP) for a dense locked Wilson core, with RG convergence controlling the quotient expansion.
control_decision.reason: The branch has a sharper nonformal analytic target: compute H and K for reflected Wilson hairpin blocks, instead of restating the closed-cone topology.

dependency_updates.description: The closed-cone passage proves collar positivity, but full same-theory OS positivity now reduces to finite quotient positivity plus the tangent-cone tests for H,K.
The locked algebra must contain Wilson hairpin collars and their finite linear combinations; otherwise the tangent falsifier may be invisible to the realized cone.
The topology must give operator-norm convergence of every finite reflected quotient block, not merely distributional convergence away from the reflection plane.
Compute first and second boundary coefficients for reflected Wilson products after diagonal normalization and same-theory factor extraction.

falsifiers: falsifier: a locked finite Wilson block with y in 1^perp and y^*Hy<0 produces an immediate negative OS determinant.
falsifier: if PHP has a null vector y and y^*(PKP-n^{-2}PH11^*HP)y<0, second-order collar collapse breaks same-theory positivity.
falsifier: a nonmultiplicative or indefinite additive boundary contact invalidates q_delta=hat N_delta oslash hat B_delta as the target OS matrix.
falsifier: the required boundary OPE exists only after adding a reflection-plane counterterm or changing Wilson-loop renormalization.
falsifier: RG convergence is valid for separated collars but too weak to control the finite reflected boundary quotient expansion.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 221 corrected the tangent-cone bridge into a precise finite-matrix statement. With the all-ones normalization E=11^*, the second-order correction is n^{-2}PH11^*HP, equivalently n^{-1}PHee^*HP for the unit constant vector e. This makes the falsifier valid and normalization-safe: one-body Wilson renormalizations vanish on 1^perp, while genuine mixed boundary OPE data survive as H and the Schur-corrected K.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Work out a three-hairpin reflected Wilson boundary OPE ansatz, extract H and K after diagonal normalization, and test the zero-sum vector (1,-1,0) and a triangle null vector for the Schur-corrected second-order form.
